questions.stem: Prepare a complete PAL fitting and ordering plan for a first-time presbyope who spends six hours daily on a computer, drives in the evening and wants a shallow frame. Explain design choice, frame checks, measurements and counselling.
questions.explanation: A general-purpose PAL should cover driving, with a design chosen to preserve useful intermediate width; a separate office lens may be discussed if computer demand is dominant. The shallow frame must pass the manufacturer's cut-out. After final adjustment, monocular PDs and separate heights are taken. At delivery, the wearer is taught distance, corridor and near use and warned not to judge the lens before technical verification and reasonable adaptation.

questions.stem: A previous successful PAL wearer reports that the new pair is swimmy, near is narrow and reading is displaced to the right. Write a systematic troubleshooting plan and identify the most likely checks before remake.
questions.explanation: Restore the markings first and verify that right and left lenses were not swapped. Compare monocular PDs and heights on the patient with the order, then check frame level, pantoscopic tilt, wrap and vertex distance. Verify Rx and add at the correct reference points and compare the prior successful design. The lateral reading displacement strongly points to PD or lens identity; swim and narrow near can also follow height, wrap or design changes. Adjust valid frame errors, otherwise remake with corrected data.
